headline: High-risk default interaction: shared MCP/tooling and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure between the agents.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can use runtime-injected MCPs/hooks and broad network egress, while Agent B uses MCP servers and stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible instruction-bridging path if A’s outputs are fed into B or a shared MCP channel exists. The pair is not directly documented interacting, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF A’s output is copied into B’s prompt or MCP input without provenance checks, injection risk is active.
IF both agents share an MCP server or message channel, attacker-controlled content can steer B.
mitigations: Disable automatic prompt forwarding between agents.
Add provenance tags to all A→B content.
Restrict B to allowlisted MCP servers only.
Review any shared clipboard or queue wiring.
requires-engineering: insert instruction/content separators in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches session history, project code, and provider authentication data, and has broad network egress; B touches financial and licensed data and can call MCP/REST APIs. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive material can flow from one agent into the other’s outputs or remote calls. No shared filesystem is explicitly documented, so this remains medium.
conditions: IF A and B run under the same OS account or workspace, file-based leakage becomes active.
IF B is given A’s session history or auth prompts, sensitive data can be exfiltrated via B’s APIs.
mitigations: Separate OS users or containers for each agent.
Remove secrets from any shared workspace.
Disable API access for B on sensitive runs.
Rotate any provider credentials used by A.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can spawn subprocesses and has broad egress; B cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, so direct write-write conflict is limited. The main overlap is shared MCP/API usage, which can still collide on mutable remote resources if both target the same service. Because B lacks local write powers, the blast radius is smaller than medium.
conditions: IF both agents target the same remote account, API quota, or MCP-backed resource, conflicting updates can occur.
IF A is configured to write files in a shared directory, local contention increases.
mitigations: Assign separate API keys or accounts.
Serialize access to shared remote resources.
Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Monitor for rate-limit or conflict errors.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared MCP resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can produce code/search results and B can consume data through MCP/REST APIs, so A’s output may become B’s input without a verification step. B is a financial-modeling agent, making downstream mistakes potentially consequential even if not directly irreversible. The pairwise pathway is plausible from profiles alone, but not directly observed, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B treats A-generated text, code, or citations as authoritative, errors cascade.
IF A’s browser-derived content is passed into B without validation, B may act on false premises.
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A outputs.
Add a verification step for all A→B facts.
Limit B to read-only analysis on A-produced artifacts.
Log source provenance for every transferred item.
requires-engineering: implement confidence/verification gates in the orchestrator.

E_compliance.rationale: A handles provider authentication data and session history, while B handles financial and licensed data. If EU PII, secrets, or regulated financial records are routed through A’s broad-egress environment or into B’s API-backed workflows, retention and residency obligations can diverge. No explicit residency or certification mismatch is documented, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is sent through A’s networked tooling, retention/residency controls may be violated.
IF B processes personal or licensed data under a stricter policy than A, compliance mismatch is active.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of A’s prompts and browser sessions.
Route sensitive data only through approved B workflows.
Document retention settings for both agents.
Use separate tenants for different data classes.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing and audit logs.
